checks: At each actual interior index, F+a_(i−1) and F−a_i are the neighboring positive tail sums. If a_(i−1)≤a_i, their mean is at most F, so scalar power concavity and monotonicity apply.

In the decreasing case δ>0 and all subsequent root increments are ≤−δ. Positivity at i+1 forces q>1, so the predecessor applies even when q is arbitrarily near one. The pointwise envelope includes a_i exactly and bounds every subsequent mass on the actual support, with zero actual mass thereafter.

Shifting the finite positive-part sum up by one adds (q+1)^d and shifting down removes q^d. The scaling δ^d identifies the two neighboring envelope tail values exactly. The parent midpoint inequality yields the envelope inequality after multiplying by δ^(dp).

H is concave and continuous up to 1/b with H(0)=0. For 0<u≤v≤1/b, concavity yields H(v)/v≤H(u)/u. Thus the nonpositive sign at u=1/F_max persists at v=1/F, and multiplying by F^p recovers the midpoint inequality at the actual tail.

Singletons and two-point supports have no tested midpoint. For longer support the actual endpoint r has F_r=a_r>0. Appending a zero would change the statement: at d=1, masses (4,1) would give the nonconcave triple (sqrt(5),1,0).
For the affine positive roots r+1−i, reversing the suffix gives the arithmetic sequence with ρ=1 exactly. A failed midpoint m≥1 for any exponent above 1/(d+1) maps to i=r−m with 0<i<r when r≥m+1.
